learn.hook: The air you breathe, the water you drink and the sunshine on your face are gifts from nature. They are nature's treasures!
points: Natural resources are useful things we get from nature, like air, water, sunlight, soil, forests, minerals, coal and petroleum.
Things made by people from natural resources, like plastic, glass, paper and cement, are human-made materials.

Air is a mixture of gases: about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen, with small amounts of others like carbon dioxide and water vapour. We need oxygen to breathe; plants use carbon dioxide to make food.
Soil forms very, very slowly as rocks break down over many years; it holds plants and gives them water and minerals.
The Sun is the main source of energy on Earth: it gives light and warmth, and plants use sunlight to make food.

example.q: Is a wooden chair a natural resource?
steps: The wood comes from trees in forests, which are natural resources.
But the chair itself was cut, shaped and joined by people.
So the wood is natural, while the chair is a human-made object.
example.answer: No. The wood is a natural resource, but the chair is made by people from it.

learn.reallife: Farmers depend on soil, water and sunlight; fishing families on the coast of Kerala depend on the sea; and the paper in your notebook came from trees.

quiz.q: Which of these is a natural resource?
quiz.explain: Water comes directly from nature. Plastic, glass and cement are made by people.
quiz.mistake: Thinks things made from natural materials are natural resources

quiz.q: Which gas makes up the largest part of air?
quiz.explain: Nitrogen is about 78% of air; oxygen is about 21%.
quiz.mistake: Thinks oxygen is the largest part of air

quiz.q: About what percentage of air is oxygen?
quiz.explain: Oxygen makes up about 21% of air.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the share of oxygen with that of nitrogen

quiz.q: What is the main source of energy for life on Earth?
quiz.explain: The Sun gives light and heat, and plants use sunlight to make food for all living things.
quiz.mistake: Picks a source made or used by people

quiz.q: How is soil formed?
options: Very slowly, as rocks break down over many years
quiz.explain: Soil forms very slowly as rocks break into tiny bits mixed with remains of plants and animals.
quiz.mistake: Thinks soil forms quickly

quiz.q: Which gas do plants take in to make their food?
quiz.explain: Plants use carbon dioxide from air, water and sunlight to make food.
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants take in only oxygen

quiz.q: Paper is made from trees. Paper is:
options: A human-made material from a natural resource
quiz.explain: Trees are natural; people make paper from wood pulp.
quiz.mistake: Does not separate a natural resource from things made from it

quiz.q: Which of these do forests give us?
options: Wood, fruits, medicines and a home for wildlife
quiz.explain: Forests give many useful things and are home to many animals.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the value of forests

teach.ask: Gappu sips from a river: 'People keep talking about natural resources. What are they? Is my nest one?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Natural resources are useful things from nature, like air, water, soil and sunlight. My nest is made by me from twigs!
teach.nudge: Where do natural resources come from? Can you name some?

learn.hook: Some treasures refill themselves, like sunlight every day. Others took millions of years to form and will run out!
points: Renewable resources are replaced by nature in a short time, or will not run out: sunlight, wind, and water (renewed by the water cycle). Forests are renewable only if we plant new trees as we cut.
Non-renewable resources took a very long time to form and cannot be replaced quickly once used up: coal, petroleum, natural gas and minerals.
Coal, petroleum and natural gas are called fossil fuels. They formed from the remains of plants and animals buried deep under the Earth over millions of years.
Burning fossil fuels gives energy but also releases smoke and gases that pollute air.
Solar panels and windmills use renewable energy. India has big solar parks and wind farms.

example.q: Why is coal called non-renewable when the Earth still has a lot of it?
steps: Coal took millions of years to form from buried plants.
We are using it much, much faster than it can form again.
Once used up, it cannot be replaced in our lifetime.
example.answer: Because it takes millions of years to form, so it cannot be replaced once we use it up.

learn.reallife: Rooftop solar panels on homes and schools turn sunlight into electricity, and windmills along the coasts of Tamil Nadu and Gujarat use wind.

quiz.q: Which is a renewable resource?
quiz.explain: The Sun keeps shining, so sunlight will not run out.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up renewable and non-renewable

quiz.q: Which is a non-renewable resource?
quiz.explain: Coal took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced quickly.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything found in large amounts is renewable

quiz.q: How were fossil fuels formed?
options: From sunlight in a few days
From remains of plants and animals buried over millions of years
quiz.explain: Buried remains changed slowly under heat and pressure into coal, petroleum and natural gas.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the origin of fossil fuels

quiz.q: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
quiz.explain: Natural gas, like coal and petroleum, is a fossil fuel.
quiz.mistake: Confuses fossil fuels with renewable energy

quiz.q: When can forests be called renewable?
options: Always, even if all trees are cut
Only if new trees are planted as old ones are cut
quiz.explain: Forests grow back only if we replant and cut wisely.
quiz.mistake: Thinks forests can never run out

quiz.q: Why should we use more solar and wind energy?
options: They are renewable and cause less pollution
quiz.explain: Sun and wind will not run out and do not release smoke like burning coal.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the benefits of renewable energy

quiz.q: Petrol and diesel are obtained from:
quiz.explain: Petrol and diesel are made by refining petroleum.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the different fossil fuels

quiz.q: Water is called renewable because:
options: We can make unlimited water in factories
The water cycle keeps renewing it
quiz.explain: Water evaporates, forms clouds and falls as rain again. But clean fresh water is limited, so we must still save it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks renewable means we can waste it

teach.ask: Gappu sees a coal truck and a solar panel: 'Both give energy. Why do people say one will run out and the other won't?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Sunlight and wind are renewable, but coal is a non-renewable fossil fuel that took millions of years to form!
teach.nudge: Why can't coal be replaced quickly? What makes sunlight different?

learn.hook: If we keep taking from nature's treasure box without care, it will become empty. Let's be smart treasure keepers!
points: Conservation means using natural resources carefully so they last for future generations.
Reduce (use less), Reuse (use again) and Recycle (make new things from old) help save resources.
Save water: turn off taps, fix leaks, and collect rainwater (rainwater harvesting). Save electricity: switch off lights and fans when not needed.
Plant trees and protect forests. In the 1970s, villagers in the hills of present-day Uttarakhand hugged trees to stop them from being cut; this was the Chipko movement.
Walk, cycle or use public transport for short trips to save fuel and keep the air cleaner.

example.q: Anu's family wants to save water at home. Which ideas work?
steps: Turn off the tap while brushing teeth.
Use a bucket instead of a running hose to wash the car, and reuse water from washing vegetables to water plants.
example.answer: All of these save water: closing taps, fixing leaks and reusing water.

learn.reallife: Van Mahotsav, a tree-planting festival held every July in India, encourages people to plant trees. Many schools and homes now collect rainwater from rooftops.

games.title: Treasure keeper quiz
items: Conservation means using resources carefully so they last.
That is the meaning of conservation.
Leaving lights on in an empty room saves electricity.
It wastes electricity; switch them off.
Rainwater harvesting collects and stores rainwater.
It helps refill underground water and gives water for later.
The Chipko movement was about hugging trees to protect them.
Villagers hugged trees to stop them from being cut.
Recycling means throwing waste into a river.
Recycling means making new things from used materials.
Cycling to a nearby shop saves fuel.
A bicycle uses no petrol or diesel.

quiz.q: What does conservation of natural resources mean?
options: Using them carefully so they last for the future
Using them as fast as possible
quiz.explain: Conservation is careful, wise use so resources last.
quiz.mistake: Thinks conservation means not using resources at all, or using them fast

quiz.q: Using an old jam jar as a pencil holder is an example of:
quiz.explain: Using the same object again for another purpose is reusing.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up reuse and recycle

quiz.q: Turning old newspapers into new paper is:
quiz.explain: Recycling turns used materials into new products.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up recycle and reuse

quiz.q: What was the Chipko movement?
options: Villagers hugging trees to stop them from being cut
quiz.explain: In the 1970s, villagers in the hills of present-day Uttarakhand hugged trees to protect forests.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the movement's purpose

quiz.q: Which is a good way to save water?
options: Turning off the tap while brushing
Washing a scooter with a running hose for an hour
quiz.explain: Closing the tap while brushing saves many litres of water.
quiz.mistake: Picks a wasteful habit

quiz.q: What is rainwater harvesting?
options: Collecting and storing rainwater for later use
Drinking rainwater straight from the roof
quiz.explain: Rooftop rainwater is collected in tanks or sent underground to recharge wells.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of harvesting rainwater

quiz.q: Which habit helps save fuel?
options: Taking a car for every small trip
Keeping the scooter engine running while waiting
Cycling or walking for short distances
quiz.explain: Cycling and walking use no fuel and keep the air cleaner.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect transport choices with fuel use

quiz.q: Carrying a cloth bag to the market instead of taking new plastic bags helps to:
quiz.explain: Using less plastic means less waste. That is 'reduce'.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how small choices reduce waste

teach.ask: Gappu worries: 'If people keep using up water and trees, will there be none left for my chicks? What can we do?'
teach.praise: Hooray! We can conserve resources by reducing, reusing and recycling, saving water and electricity and planting trees!
teach.nudge: What are the three R's? And what can we do every day to save water or electricity?
